main_text.l: tum de arte in tertia significatione accepta : quanquam
etiam de illa dubitatur, vtrum semper operetur in externam
& corpoream materiam, & ex ea opus corporeum efficiat, vt a-
libi disceptari solet. Proinde mirum non est, si Metaphy-
sica talis ars non sit.
4 Vtrum Metaphysica sit disciplina contemplatrix,
an operatrix?
DVo sunt summa genera disciplinarum. Vnum con-
templatricium, alterum operatricium, vt scite ad-
modum docet Zabarella lib. 1 de natura Logicæ, cap. 2.
Recte igitur quæritur, ad quod genus Metaphysica sit refe-
renda? Quoniam vero illa res sibi subiectas considerat
non operationis gratia, vt scilicet homo rerum cognita-
rum [?]θεωρίαν, vel agendo, vel efficiendo moliatur; sed
solum cognitionis causa, vt videlicet homo naturalem
sciendi appetitum iucundissima rerum metaphysica-
rum notitia expleat, & viam sibi ad alias disciplinas pla-
nam & expeditam sternat ac præparet: idcirco Meta-
physica non ad genus disciplinarum operatricium, sed
contemplatricium est referenda. Neque obstat quod su-
pra a nobis definita fuit per artem. Sicut enim scientia,
ita etiam ars in generali significatione alia est
ϑεωρητικὴ[?], alia πρακτικὴ[?], alia ποιητικὴ[?]. Ideoque vt intelligeretur, in
quo genere artis Metaphysica sit ponenda, adiunctum
fuit, quod sit ars contemplatiua.
5 Quod sit proprium & adæquatum subiectum
Metaphysicæ?
MAgna est controuersia inter Philosophos de
subiecto proprio & adæquato Metaphysicæ. Cum
enim illud constet ex re consideratâ & modo conside-
randi, de vtraque parte diuersæ hinc inde opiniones re-
periuntur. Nam quod ad rem consideratam attinet, il-
lam alii statuunt solum Deum; alii substantiam incor-
poream, quatenus suo ambitu complectitur Deum &
creaturas spirituales; alii omne ens reale commune Deo &
creaturæ, substantiæ & accidenti: alii denique omne ens
tam reale quam rationis. Sed nulla harum quatuor sen-
tentiarum idetur penitus exprimere totam rei in Me-
taphysica [?]consideratæ vniuersitatem.- Metaphysicus e-
nim non tantum contemplatur ens, sed etiam non ens,
adeoque

marginalia.note: Res considerata in Metaphysica quæ sit.

page.notes: Doubtful readings: the Greek words at the start of the section 4 paragraph and in the "Sicut enim" sentence (ϑεωρίαν, ϑεωρητικὴ, πρακτικὴ, ποιητικὴ) are hard to read at this scan resolution; accents and breathings are uncertain. "idetur" in the last paragraph may be a printing error for "videtur" (kept as printed, marked as a doubtful word on the following line). The word "consideratæ" is partly obscured by a stain and by the faint letters near the line end. Marginal notes on the left are transcribed in full, placed beside the lines where they stand. Printing irregularities such as the dash after "vniuersitatem" are left as printed. Right margin, lower right corner, and the digitiser's watermark are excluded.
